claims.explanation: Vinorelbine is a tubulin-polymerization inhibitor, so selectivity is most likely driven by the cellular context that determines mitotic dependency and drug efflux/handling rather than by a single lineage. The pattern of sensitive lines is enriched for TP53-mutant, highly proliferative carcinomas (gastric, endometrial, lung, melanoma), while several resistant lines carry EGFR-activating mutations or intact p53-pathway/less mitotically driven states, suggesting that loss of p53-mediated arrest and high mitotic rate sensitize, whereas EGFR-driven or low-proliferation contexts protect.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is highly enriched in the most-killed lines and impairs mitotic checkpoint/apoptotic arrest after microtubule poisoning
Activating EGFR mutations appear in several least-affected NSCLC lines and EGFR signaling promotes survival/proliferation independent of microtubule integrity
BRAF-mutant melanoma/endometrial lines are among the most killed, consistent with MAPK-driven high mitotic dependency
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines and may increase PI3K/AKT-driven proliferation and mitotic dependence
KRAS-mutant colorectal, pancreatic, ovarian and gastric lines are enriched among sensitive lines
High beta-III tubulin expression is a known mediator of resistance to tubulin-polymerization inhibitors such as vinorelbine
Altered tubulin isotype expression can reduce vinorelbine binding and microtubule destabilization
CDKN2A loss appears in sensitive melanoma/bone lines and releases cells into unchecked proliferation
ATM mutation appears in sensitive endometrial/ovarian lines and may impair DNA-damage responses after mitotic stress
NF1 loss in sensitive thyroid/upper-aerodigestive lines may increase RAS/MAPK-driven proliferation
ARID1A mutation appears in several sensitive endometrial/bladder lines and may alter chromatin-dependent mitotic gene programs
STK11 mutation appears in least-affected ovarian/kidney/glioma lines and may reduce metabolic/mitotic stress sensitivity
